thread:
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert fired (incident: SLO-P95-BURN) — 6 services affected in us-west, current p95 ~2.8s (> target 1.2s). Pager: Ken

sre-bot: autocontext: alert group: latency.slo.p95; src=obs; threshold=20m of p95>1.2s; count=6; hostgroups: inference-serving-us-west

Ken: acked the page — oncall looking now

Ken: quick check — dashboards show steady CPU/GPU usage but a cluster of hosts with high queue depth (sidecar backlog). starting triage

Riley: seeing increased continous batching on 4 pods, kv-cache eviction spikes around same time. could be hotkeys.

Aisha: any customer visible errors? ProdSupport, do we have reports?

ProdSupport: two support tickets from major-customer-a describing slow responses (chat timeouts). They report increased latencies since 09:12 UTC. No errors otherwise.

Ken: rolling diagnostics now — pulling recent tail logs from pods:
```
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/runner-xyz -c sidecar --tail=200 | grep -E "evict|queue_depth|batch_size"
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z sidecar INFO queue_depth=78 batch_size=16 evict=true
2026-03-15T09:13:05Z sidecar WARN kvcache.eviction.rate=0.45
```

Ken: looks like kv-cache thrash -> larger batch sizes -> higher latency tail. Might be a hotkey or traffic shift.

sre-bot: NOTE: autoscaler has not triggered (min_replicas=3, current_replicas=3). backlog per pod > 60. Suggest scale-up.

Aisha: Ken can you temp route traffic to stable-variant v2 which has smaller batch config? I can bump replica count and enable experimental throttling on burst config.

Ken: routing change initiated: `/infra/route set inference-service -> stable-variant:v2 for 20%` (will monitor) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Riley: scaling pods from 3 -> 6 now (HPA override). Also setting sidecar max_batch=8 -> 4 on the pods via ConfigMap patch:
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap sidecar-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch":"4"}}'
```

Ken: confirmed route shift at 09:18 UTC. p95 on shifted traffic looks fine. overall p95 dropped to ~1.6s but still >1.2s due to remaining pods.

sre-bot: escalation: unacked longer than 5m -> paging escalation to SRE lead (Aisha).

Aisha: acked escalation. I'll own mitigation and customer comms. Riley — can you evict problematic keys from kv-cache and restart sidecar on the 4 affected pods?

Riley: evicting suspected hotkeys now, restarting sidecar containers one-by-one to avoid jank. `for pod in $(kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runner -o name | head -n4); do kubectl -n inference exec $pod -- sidecarctl evict hotkey; kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/runner-xyz; done`

ProdSupport: told customer-a we are investigating and performing mitigations; offered ETA 15-30m. Customer acknowledged :white_check_mark:

Ken: after restarts and scale, p95=1.15s, p99=2.6s, error rate unchanged. Looks like majority of customers back to normal, a small tail remains.

Aisha: that's within SLO for p95 — keep monitoring next 30m. Opening a follow-up postmortem to track root cause: likely kv-cache hotkey + packer config change. Assigning to Riley for follow-up, Ken to verify autoscaler hysteresis and disable HPA cooldown if needed.

sre-bot: incident resolved for paging workflow. If p95 rises above 1.2s again, auto-escalate to oncall lead.

Ken: thanks team — final notes: mitigations: scale bump, route 20%->stable-variant, reduce max_batch, evict hotkeys, restart sidecars. Customer impact: degraded p95 for ~12 minutes, customer-a had perceivable slowness but no data loss.

Aisha: adding timeline + logs to the incident ticket. Closing page for now. :thumbsup:
